entries.claim: The completion rule equates every trace-side `reason: ENOENT` with an absent planning root, even though `ENOENT` can also result from a broken/dangling `.planning` symlink (or the root disappearing between the seam's check and append). That lets a corrupted or unsafe planning layout take the treeless “report done” arm, contrary to the rule's stated treatment of symlink failures as reasons to withhold done.
entries.failure_scenario: Start with `.planning` as a dangling symlink, then run `/cad-task` with no landed commits or with a clean risk-check result. Trace append returns `ok:true, written:false, reason: ENOENT`; the workflow reports done as if this were an intentionally treeless repository, rather than surfacing the broken planning root and withholding completion. The new seam test only covers a genuinely absent directory, so it does not distinguish this case.
entries.counter_evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/trace.mjs:1116-1121 lstats the trace FILE and refuses a linked one as reason symlinked-trace; the withholding half in task.md names that symlinked trace, not a symlinked root. A dangling .planning symlink is an absent planning root to every reader in the tree, and task.md done step renders that ENOENT as the record unrecorded rather than as a landed receipt. Real edge, no silent loss: downgraded to low.

entries.claim: The claimed “nothing is created” seam test does not run `/cad-task` or observe filesystem operations; it manually invokes selected CLI commands and only asserts that the planning directory is absent after all calls complete. It therefore cannot prove that the workflow's treeless path creates nothing.
entries.failure_scenario: A later edit to `task.md` adds a `mkdir .planning`/config initialization before its seam calls, or a seam temporarily scaffolds `.planning` and removes it before returning. This test remains green because it never executes the workflow and its final `existsSync(dir) === false` assertion cannot detect transient creation. The advertised treeless-path guarantee can regress while all added assertions pass.
entries.counter_evidence: cadence-core/bin/planning-task-record.test.mjs:142-152 states the test scope as the mechanical half - the four seams task.md calls - and the workflow prose is pinned separately by prose-agreement.test.mjs. No seam creates the planning root (task-record.mjs answers no planning root; trace.mjs appendEvent has no mkdir). The transient-scaffold scenario names no code path and is a hypothetical future regression: downgraded to low.

entries.claim: The “in ONE place” prose pin is not global: it only rejects verdict-like wording in the `risk_check` skip paragraph and `record` step. A duplicate or contradictory completion rule added to `done`, `bracket`, or another part of `task.md` leaves this test green.
entries.failure_scenario: Someone restores an old-style statement in the `done` step such as “on `written: false` do not report done,” while leaving the new `risk_check` sentences intact. The reporting and withholding assertions still pass, as do the skip/record checks, but a treeless run again has conflicting instructions about whether it may finish.
entries.counter_evidence: cadence-core/bin/prose-agreement.test.mjs ONCE block reads stepBody(task, record) and the skip-arm paragraph only; task.md done step (line 316) points at the completion rule today but no assertion holds it there. Confirmed at low, not fixed.
